subject.title: [Feature]: Pattern-based channel allowlist for Discord (glob/wildcard support)

question: Should Discord guild channel allowlists accept glob-style channel keys such as `ws-*`, and what exact precedence should they have relative to exact channel keys, thread-parent fallback, category inheritance, and literal `*`?
rationale: This is not a broken existing contract; it adds authorization-sensitive config syntax that could widen which Discord channels can trigger agents, so automation should not choose the product and security semantics.

options.title: Approve narrow glob contract
options.body: Add Discord-owned glob matching with explicit precedence, schema/types/docs, audit/status visibility, and focused ingress tests while keeping category inheritance and access-list redesign separate.

options.title: Fold into broader Discord access work
options.body: Keep the dynamic-channel problem tied to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60582 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/69748 before implementation.

options.title: Reject glob syntax
options.body: Keep exact entries plus the literal `*` model and document that dynamic workstreams should use broad wildcard, category inheritance, or future access-control work instead.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow glob contract
recommendation.body: Add Discord-owned glob matching with explicit precedence, schema/types/docs, audit/status visibility, and focused ingress tests while keeping category inheritance and access-list redesign separate.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the shared matcher and Discord allow-list implementation that would carry the precedence decision.
